summary: Jan Willem de Jong worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. Educated at Leiden University, the Sorbonne, and Collège de France under F. B. J. Kuiper, Paul Demiéville, and others, he held chairs at Leiden and the Australian National University.

Jan-Ulrich Sobisch is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under David P. Jackson and David Seyfort Ruegg. He held posts at the Universities of Hamburg, Munich, and Copenhagen, and worked on the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project.

Jane Bunnag is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of London by 1969, where she studied under the supervision of E. Michael Mendelson and Barbara E. Ward.

Jane Ellen Harrison was a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at Newnham College under Robert Alexander Neil from circa 1874 to 1879, and later held a post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1898 to 1922.

Janet Gyatso works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. After earning her BA, MA, and PhD at UC Berkeley, she taught at Amherst College (1987–2001) and Harvard University, where she became Hershey Professor of Buddhist Studies in 2001.

Jang-Kil Chun is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. His studies were conducted under doctoral supervisor Minoru Kiyota, as well as teachers Paul J. Griffiths, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Frances A. Wilson.

Janice Dean Willis is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. She earned degrees from Cornell and Columbia (PhD under Alex Wayman) and served as a professor at Wesleyan University (1977–2013) and part-time teacher at Agnes Scott College (2014–2020).

Jann Ronis specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under doctoral supervisor David Germano and teacher Jeffrey Hopkins, and was attested in an academic post there in 2007.

Jared Rhoton was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral dissertation at Columbia University by 1985 under the supervision of Alex Wayman and also studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga.

Jarl Charpentier was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Uppsala University under Karl Ferdinand Johansson, also studying at the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He served as Assistant Professor at Uppsala from 1908, succeeding Johansson in 1927.
Jaroslav Průšek was a Czech sinologist. He pursued his higher education at Charles University, within its Faculty of Arts, from approximately 1924 to 1930.

Jason Birch is an Indologist who studied at the University of Sydney and completed his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He has held positions at Oxford (attested 2011) and SOAS University of London (attested 2020).

Jason M. Wirth is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teacher Kosho Itagaki. He held the Theiline Pigott McCone Chair in Humanities at Seattle University from 2014 to 2016.

Jason Matthew McCombs specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a BS from the University of Michigan and a PhD from UCLA under Gregory Schopen, where he was attested as a lecturer in 2014.

Jason Neelis works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of Washington under Richard Salomon. He held posts at Washington, Käte Hamburger Kolleg, and Wilfrid Laurier University as Associate Professor and Department Chair.

Jason Protass is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his PhD at Stanford University under John Kieschnick. His career includes appointments as a Fulbright Fellow at Academia Sinica and visiting researcher at Ryukoku University.

Jay Holt Valentine specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Delaware, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD at Virginia under the doctoral supervision of Kurtis R. Schaeffer.

Jay Jasanoff is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Harvard University. He held faculty posts at UC Berkeley, Cornell University as professor of linguistics (circa 1978–1998), and Harvard, becoming Diebold Professor of Indo-European Linguistics and Philology in 1998.

Jay L. Garfield is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar. He has held professorships at Smith College, Hampshire College, the University of Massachusetts Amherst, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, the University of Melbourne, and the National University of Singapore.

Jay M. Bernstein is a philosopher who studied at the University of Edinburgh (1971–1975). He held academic posts at the University of Essex (circa 1975–1996), Vanderbilt University (circa 1996–2001), and The New School (circa 2001).
